x: Everything starts here. The khyzr design system holds the tokens, assets, components and thirteen chapters of rules that every khyzr surface is built from.

Tokens are the values. Color, type, spacing, radii and motion are set in the token files, design-system/tokens/. Where any prose — a chapter, the digest, an older document — disagrees with a token, the token wins. Logos are used as files. Take the exported SVGs from design-system/assets/logos/. Never redraw a mark, recolor it, or compose symbol and name by hand. Mark colors come from the mark files, palette colors from the tokens. The site is built from the system's own files. Every swatch, specimen, download and live component here is generated from the tokens, the logo, icon and pattern files, and the React primitives. Nothing is copied by hand, so nothing can drift. Start from the tokens. design-system/styles.css is the CSS entry and imports every token file; link it and every value on this site is yours. The five React primitives run live on the Components and Forms pages, with their props. It is a working system. Decisions land at locked checkpoints. Where something has no answer yet, it says so and stays pending.

Layout, radii, hairlines and shadows, motion and spacing — the structural values.

One container, generous air. The container is container, centered, with fluid gutter margins — slim at 1080p, generous and centered above. Reading measures never track the container. Sections alternate White and surface-2; green-900 interludes punctuate them (voices, the name, the CTA band). The footer is always Ink. Reading measures stay editorial: the lede runs at measure-lede, the manifesto and long-form at measure-reading. Four corners, and nothing in between. radius-s — nav links and small chips. radius-m — cards, the nav bar, code blocks. radius-l — bands, grids, heroes. radius-pill — every button. All buttons are pills.

Flat by default, depth on demand. Resting UI is bordered, not shadowed. At rest, a surface carries a 1px hairline border and no shadow. Cards stay flat: white on white, separated by the hairline, with the alt band for rhythm. Shadows appear only on hover and on floating elements — always soft, large-blur, negative-spread. The nav in its paper state is shadowless: white at 97% over a hairline. On dark surfaces, borders are white at 10–11% (on-dark-border) and dividers white at 10% (on-dark-divider). Dark surfaces take no shadows. Shadow recipes Card, on hover 0 22px 40px −26px, Ink at 32% Button, on hover 0 14px 30px −12px, black at 55%

The Green Trace, in brief. The full grammar is the Motion page: springs move things, never colors; entrances overlap; nothing animates twice. Everything respects prefers-reduced-motion, which shows the final states. Reveal — the root-anchored rise Things grow in. An entrance rises rise-distance to rest and scales from rise-scale to 1, anchored at the element's baseline, over dur-enter on the ease-trace spring. Items in a group follow dur-stagger apart, overlapping. Springs move transforms only. Color and opacity change on a plain ease. Micro-interactions Buttons grow to 1.05 on ease-pop, dur-hover Cards lift −3px, tilt −.4°, scale 1.015 Arrows slide +4px on ease-pop Counts run dur-count, then a settle pulse to 1.07 Keyboard focus A 2px outline in focus-ring, khyzr Green, offset 3px outside the element. On dark, the outline is white. Selection Text selection tints with selection, a translucent khyzr Green.
The scale, locked in July 2026: six steps, space-1 to space-6, plus the fluid section clamps (section-pad-y, gutter). Every new value comes from the scale.

The Verdant standard — the deep green in the lead, with cobalt, marigold, terracotta and steel as working secondaries. Around it sit the functional website palette, a brand palette for design work, and the approved hero gradient.

From the logo: the four greens of the Verdant standard, adopted 2026-08-08, plus the black and the paper they sit on. One green family carries the brand; photos are never green-tinted. khyzr-green is the primary brand green. forest is the deep green for hover, pressed states and deep fills. deep-forest is the deepest solid. mint is the light sage. ink is the workhorse black, for headings. paper, the page canvas, is white since 2026-09-29. The logo art keeps its own brighter cut of the same hue — #149314 · #136E13 · #0C4A0C · #5CBA5C, the original marks' value and saturation rotated to the adopted green. Every UI color derives from the tokens. Take mark colors from the mark files and palette colors from the tokens. Never recolor either to match the other.

The functional palette the interface is built from. Greens — 050 to 900 A functional, hue-consistent scale rebuilt around the Verdant primary; its tints read sage, not mint. green-500 is khyzr Green, and it is text-safe as it stands: AA for body text on Paper, no darker twin needed. green-600 is the pressed state of the primary. green-700 is Forest and green-800 is Deep Forest. green-300 is green-bright, the accent on dark. green-100 is pale mint, also a stop in the hero gradient. green-900 carries the dark surfaces and anchors the gradient. green-400 and lighter are for graphics and large text only. Bright leaf lives only in the gradient. It is not part of the scale. Secondaries True secondaries, not just functional. Cobalt informs, marigold warms, terracotta signals, steel quiets. Use them creatively across pages and designs — accents, washes, graphic moments — as long as green reads first. Never set them side by side as competing fields, and never let one carry the brand. Data-viz discipline is unchanged: green is series 1, and terracotta only flags. Grades are measured on Paper. Where a color can't carry copy, its darkened text twin is named, and the twin governs it as copy. cobalt info the one text-safe secondary marigold highlight graphics only — text uses marigold-text terracotta signal large text only — text uses terracotta-text steel wash and quiet data text uses steel-text Neutrals The canvas, surfaces and text greys. paper is the page background; surface carries cards; surface-2 carries the alternate sections; hairline draws the borders. faint is for captions, muted for secondary text, body for body text, ink for headings. The text greys keep a green cast. The canvas, the alt surface and the hairline are neutral since 2026-09-29, so cards on the canvas separate by their hairline. pitch is a surface color — dark sections and the gradient anchor. It is never a text color. On dark Text on Ink, Pitch and green-900 surfaces: the footer, the statement bands. Locked 2026-07-08. on-dark-heading for headings, on-dark-soft for statement text, on-dark-body for footer links and body, on-dark-muted for secondary text, on-dark-faint for labels and legal. on-dark-accent is green-bright, for the accent word. Dividers on dark are on-dark-divider, white at 10%; borders are on-dark-border, white at 11%. Functional roles How color is allowed to touch the UI. Link, te

For brand design — decks, social, print, motion. These are named colors, not tokens. Greens dominate; the secondaries are moments, one at a time. Each field has its sanctioned type pairing: Pitch Mint or Pale Mint Deep Forest Pale Mint or Paper Forest Pale Mint or White khyzr Green White Mint Deep Forest Pale Mint Forest or Deep Forest Paper Ink, with hairline borders Cobalt White Marigold Deep Forest or Ink Terracotta White, large only Steel White, large only A working ratio, not law: Paper 46% · Pitch 18% · Deep Forest 12% · khyzr Green 12% · Mint 7% · Pale Mint 5%.

The hero ramp is a brand-approved artifact. Use it as shipped; don't derive UI colors from it. Bright leaf exists only in this ramp. Pitch doubles as the dark-surface neutral. It runs top to bottom: pitch, deep green, forest, bright leaf, mint, pale mint, white. gradient-hero interpolates in OKLab; gradient-hero-srgb is the same ramp interpolated in sRGB. On the hero itself the ramp is drawn in a shader. The token is its flat equivalent, for use anywhere else.

Every pair, measured. WCAG 2.1 ratios are computed from the tokens, not eyeballed. The floors: 4.5:1 for text (AA); 3:1 for large text (24px and up, or bold from 19px) and for graphics; 7:1 for AAA. Floors in force Reading copy is body or muted, never faint. Faint is for captions and labels. green-700 is available for emphatic text. Marigold never sets text; its twin marigold-text does. Terracotta text always uses the twin terracotta-text. Terracotta itself is for chart marks, flags and large text. Cobalt is the only text-safe secondary. The steel tint (viz-4) is a chart shape beside labelled values, never text. On green-900: white for headings, on-dark-body and on-dark-soft for reading, on-dark-muted for labels and legal, green-bright for accent words. Terracotta is marks only on dark; steel and the steel tint serve as graphics. muted and cobalt never sit on green-900 — they sink. Badges set Deep Forest on Pale Mint. The primary also passes on Pale Mint, so badge text may go primary or Deep Forest. A signal chip sets the text twin on the terracotta wash (signal-tint), bold or large only.
Four faces, each with one job. Outfit is the one family, carrying display, text and UI; Manrope is the technical register; one serif accent; the name in Arabic.

The cast. Since 2026-09-19 the system runs on one family: Outfit carries display, text and UI, and Manrope took over the technical labels when JetBrains Mono was retired. Outfit, display (font-display). The hero word, titles, ledes, quotes, pillars, taglines. Geometric, tight tracking. Locked as the display face on 2026-07-08. Outfit, text and UI (font-text). Body copy, buttons, nav links, captions. The workhorse — everything that isn't display or a technical label. Manrope, the technical register (font-tech). Eyebrows, labels, numerals and indices, lanes, footer headings, the scroll cue, chart axes and captions. Small technical text only, 11–13px, never a sentence. Always uppercase, always wide-tracked — the only place uppercase is allowed outside the hero word. Section eyebrows are numbered in this register: "01 · What we do". Instrument Serif, the editorial accent (font-serif-accent). Italic only, lowercase — one human moment per page. Never for body copy or headings. Noto Naskh Arabic, the name (font-arabic). Reserved for the name moment — الخضر, Al-Khidr, "the Green One." It appears at most once per surface, and nowhere else. Browser and app chrome are exempt. No monospace JetBrains Mono is retired; the system has no monospace. The old font-mono alias is gone — use font-tech. Space Grotesk is not part of the system. The product sites follow the same decision: khyzr.ai and khyzr.studio are Outfit-only and load no Manrope. khyzr.com keeps its eyebrows in Manrope. Webfonts are Google-hosted for now; there are no local font files yet.

The steps in use, fluid, rendered live at this viewport. The type tokens are the source of truth. Hero word text-hero-word display at fw-display, uppercase, −0.02em Title text-title display at fw-display, tracking-display, line-height 1.02 Feature quote text-quote display at fw-display, −0.022em, line-height 1.16 Lede text-lede text at fw-text, line-height 1.55, in muted Body text-body text at fw-text, line-height 1.55–1.6 Eyebrow text-eyebrow tech at 600, uppercase, tracking-eyebrow, with the green dash Label text-label tech at 600, uppercase, .10em; numbers tabular

How type behaves. One green word Titles get at most one word in khyzr Green — usually the last, usually the payoff: in "One team.", the green falls on "team." Sentence case everywhere Headings and body are sentence case, and headlines end with periods when they are sentences. Uppercase belongs to the technical labels and the hero word only. Tight up top, open below Display tracks negative, −0.02 to −0.03em; titles take tracking-display. Technical labels track wide — tracking-eyebrow on eyebrows, .10em on labels. Body stays neutral. Manrope sets wider than the retired mono did, so its tracking came down with the change. Serif is a spice Instrument Serif italic appears once per page at most — a human aside, never structure. Weights by role Weights are set by role, never by eye: fw-display for display, fw-ui for UI, fw-text for prose. Emphasis inside body is 600, never italics. Display face, locked Outfit is the display face, full stop. TWK Everett is not part of the system.
How khyzr sounds and how its copy is written: the personality, the eight rules, the mechanics, the words, and the name.

Approachable. Transparent. Dependable. The brand looks enterprise-formal; the person you meet in the writing is human. First person "we", direct "you". No exclamation marks, no hype adjectives, no emoji, ever.

Approachable, transparent, dependable, in every sentence. Talk like a human. Plain, conversational sentences. No copywriter punctuation: no em-dash constructions, no colon-heavy headlines. Empathetic, never accusatory. The buyer's past choices were reasonable. Concrete over metaphor. Say what actually happens: "the work comes back in separate pieces from separate teams," not "silos." Calm and assured, never scrappy or underdog. khyzr has reach; write like it. Forward-motion language. The brand moves things; sentences should too. Never frame the relationship as ending. No "when we're done," no "we leave you with." Permanence is earned, not declared, so we never declare it either; we just never write the goodbye. Candor as integrity. We tell you what we see, not what you want to hear.

The signature moves. The turn. The sentence ends on a reversal: "…what we see, not what you want to hear." One turn per paragraph, at most. The callback. One phrase may recur per page, as an echo, not a chorus. The reassure. Every big CTA gets a stakes-lowering line beneath it: "A short conversation to see if we're the right fit." Ask, then soften. Long–short rhythm. A flowing sentence, then a clipped one: "It's never just one thing." The short sentence carries the weight. Two-beat headlines. Period-terminated pairs: "Every discipline. One team." · "Strive Forward. Thrive Together." The second beat gets the green word. Numbered eyebrows. Section eyebrows are numbered and set in the technical register: "01 · What we do".

CTAs. The primary CTA is always "Book a conversation", never "Get started", "Learn more", "Contact us" or "Book a demo". Text links are verb-first and carry the arrow: "See the work →". On screen the arrow is the arrow-right icon, not a typed character (see Icons). Casing. Sentence case everywhere, headlines included; the tagline keeps its own casing. Headlines end with periods when they're sentences. Uppercase exists only in the technical register's labels and the hero word. Punctuation. No exclamation marks, no emoji, no ellipses, and none of the copywriter's em-dash constructions. Middle dots (·) join taxonomy labels: "Finance · Accounting". Labels and numerals. Set in the technical register (font-tech), uppercase and tracked, never a monospace. Disciplines are numbered 01–06. Lanes read like a taxonomy, not a tagline: "Healthcare AI", "Brand · Marketing · Design". Claims. Confidence without superlatives about ourselves. We describe what we do and let restraint carry the status; the copy never begs. Taglines. "Everything starts here." opens; "Strive Forward. Thrive Together.", the carried verbal asset, closes and signs the © line. Don't coin new taglines per page.

"Alongside your team", not "inside yours," not "for you." Completion is the client's felt outcome, never outbound copy. We never tell a client their business is incomplete without us. "The everything company" is internal shorthand and qualified-room sales language; on public surfaces the promise is the whole board, not "anything for anyone." Lean on ally · alongside · one team · the whole board · go deep · clarity · guide · stronger than we found them Never synergy · empower · unlock · world-class · cutting-edge · disrupt · end-to-end · seamless · the exclamation mark · emoji
Not this, then this. Get in touch to learn more! Book a conversation. Silos. The work comes back in separate pieces from separate teams.

Al-Khidr, "the Green One": الخضر The name is told once per surface, with its story: the sage people sought when the path wasn't clear — an advisor, not a ruler. He came in, guided, and moved on. The Arabic name appears at most once per surface, and only in that moment, under the kicker "The name". It is set in Noto Naskh Arabic. Never as decoration, never sprinkled through copy. Browser and app chrome are exempt. Elsewhere, the company is simply khyzr — always lowercase, and so are its products: khyzr.ai, khyzr.studio. That holds in copy, titles, meta, alt and aria text; code identifiers and file names keep their own spelling. Never "Khyzr", never "khyzr Consulting Group".
The corporate marks — wordmark, symbol, lockups and badges — and the product marks for khyzr.ai and khyzr.studio. The name leads; the symbol stands alone only where the name can't fit.

The wordmark is the primary mark and the default signature everywhere. Use khyzr-wordmark_on-light.svg on light surfaces and khyzr-wordmark_on-dark.svg on dark ones. On the site, the on-dark wordmark brands the nav and the footer. The glowing green dot is an accent motif, not a brand mark.

s: The symbol, where the name can't fit
x: The symbol stands alone only where the name can't fit: favicons, avatars, tight squares. khyzr-symbol_on-light.svg on light surfaces, khyzr-symbol_on-dark.svg on dark ones. Below 24px the symbol never appears bare; the badge carries it (see below).

Symbol and name together, for generous room. With room, use the exported lockups: horizontal (lockup-h) or vertical (lockup-v), each on light and on dark. Never compose symbol and name by hand. New lockups are cut from the masters only, on request.

The marks are not drawn in the palette's greens. They carry exactly four fills — the logo cut of the brand hue: #149314 · #136E13 · #0C4A0C · #5CBA5C. That is the original marks' value and saturation, with the hue matched to the adopted green; every UI color comes from the tokens. Take mark colors from the mark files and palette colors from the tokens. Never recolor either to match the other. No tints, no strokes, no recolored variants beyond this set. These rules govern the corporate mark. The product marks are their own set (see Product marks).

The symbol is never reproduced in one color — the four greens are the mark. Engraving, embossing, single-color print, fax: use khyzr-wordmark_black.svg or khyzr-wordmark_white.svg. Black and white wordmarks only where color can't print or render. There is no mono symbol, and none will be cut.

On-light files for paper and other white surfaces; on-dark files for ink and pitch. Marks sit on paper (white), ink, pitch or the deep green, green-900. Never on the gradient's mid-greens. Never on photography without a solid field.
The floors are locked. Symbol 24px Wordmark 90px wide Lockups 120px wide Clearspace is one blade of the symbol, on all sides.

Under the symbol's 24px floor — favicons, avatars, app tiles — the mark appears only on a plate. The default is the green-900 plate: khyzr-symbol_on-dark_badge.svg. On black or near-black surroundings the plate is white: khyzr-symbol_on-light_badge.svg (amended 2026-09-29). Favicon. One file for every theme, khyzr-favicon.svg: the green-900 plate in a light browser, the white plate in a dark one. It switches by prefers-color-scheme. Avatars. The badge fills the circle, cropped edge to edge — LinkedIn, X, Slack. Never the bare symbol. Share cards (og:image, 1200×630). A green-900 field, <khyzr-pattern> at seed 7 and scale .4, and the exported lockup-h centered. No taglines below 20px. The badge is not a mono variant. It is the full-color mark on its plate; mono contexts still mean the wordmark.

The mark is registered. The default files are the non-® set; the ® set lives in design-system/assets/logos/reg/. Use the ® set where the use is prominent, formal or legal: contracts, packaging, first prominent use. Footer yes, navbar no.

Every logo file follows one pattern: khyzr-[asset]_[background]_[flags]_[size].[ext]. All lowercase; hyphens inside a field, underscores between fields; no spaces; never the ® character in a filename. Backgrounds are on-light and on-dark. The mono wordmark puts its ink in that slot instead: black for light grounds, white for dark ones. The no-® file is the base; _reg flags the version carrying ®. Raster sizes come last: khyzr-symbol_on-dark_512.png. The field order is fixed, so files sort into families. The SVG set in the design system is the working set. The EPS, PDF and PNG masters are kept with the logo masters.

khyzr.ai and khyzr.studio each carry a product wordmark and a product icon. Each product has its own page with its files, colours and cuts: [khyzr.ai](../khyzr-ai/) and [khyzr.studio](../khyzr-studio/). The corporate rules above are unchanged and govern the corporate mark. Icon or wordmark, never both. There are no product lockups. The icon covers favicons, avatars, app tiles and square spaces; the wordmark covers everything else. The wordmark is the corporate wordmark, path data unchanged, followed by .ai or .studio in Outfit 500, outlined. The x-heights match, the word is tracked −.02em, and both sit on the wordmark's own baseline. Unlike the corporate wordmark files, the product wordmarks tint the wordmark. The icon is the corporate symbol in the product's own ramp, keeping the corporate structure: the back pair (top left), the middle four, and the front pair (bottom right, on top). Like the corporate symbol, it is never one color. The tiles follow the corporate badge. green-900 is the brand hue taken very dark; each product tile is that product's flagship hue at the same lightness. On black or near-black surroundings the tile turns white and the icon takes its light cut. The product favicons keep the deep tile in every browser, light or dark. At the product sites' nav size the wordmark sets at 35.4px, under the corporate 90px floor. The icons in use Each product's icon, alone and on its tiles, and its favicon. The icon is the tab, the app tile and the avatar; wherever the name has room, the wordmark takes over, and the two are never set side by side. Favicon: the deep-tile badge, in light and dark browsers alike: one SVG per product, with a 32px PNG for browsers that take no SVG. App icon and avatar: the deep-tile badge cropped full-bleed, so the platform rounds it. Still open Floor and clearspace for the product marks: TBD — not yet decided. Whether the brand kit and the employee Drive carry the product marks: TBD — not yet decided.
One icon family, Solar, in two weights — Linear for the utility tier, Line Duotone for the illustrative tier. Utility works; illustrative speaks.

One family — Solar, by 480 Design (MIT) — in two weights. Utility · Solar Linear Quiet strokes that do work: navigation, actions, form states. 16–24px, stroke 1.5, a single color. ink or body on light; white or green-bright (green-300) on dark. Inline with text or in buttons. Illustrative · Solar Line Duotone The same geometry plus a 20% layer, reserved for feature moments: discipline markers, section leads, empty states. 32px or larger, one per card or section. forest on light, green-bright on dark. The 20% layer rides along.

The set covers what the site actually uses — nothing speculative. Nine utility icons, six illustrative. Utility A 24 grid, stroke 1.5, currentColor. Illustrative Semantic names, and the swap target for bespoke icons. Illustrative files carry semantic names: strategy.svg, not compass.svg. When bespoke icons arrive, they replace files one for one, and every surface updates.

Inherit color through currentColor — ink or body on light, white or green-bright on dark, forest for duotone on light Mix suites — no Lucide, Phosphor, or leftover glyph fonts Utility at 16–24px; illustrative at 32px or larger Shrink illustrative icons below 32px — the 20% layer muddies One illustrative icon per card or section — it marks the moment Recolor the duotone layer independently, or add fills Keep semantic filenames; bespoke icons replace files one for one Use icons for brand marks — LinkedIn, X and partners are logos No emoji, and no unicode characters standing in for icons.
Discipline markers take the illustrative icons, in duotone, green-bright on dark. Row and link arrows are arrow-right. The external-link mark is arrow-right-up. Both arrows replace the typed → and ↗.

Masters live in design-system/assets/icons/, split into utility/ and illustrative/. Every file is sized 1em wide and high and draws in currentColor. Source: Solar by 480 Design, under the MIT licence.
Honest documentary. Real people mid-work, real rooms, natural light — photography as evidence that we're actually there.

Candid, calm, uncorrected. Photos are the human register; the green stays in UI, pattern and type. The direction was adopted on 2026-07-13. Grade: saturate(.88) contrast(1.02). That's the whole grade, fixed for every photo. No green cast, no HDR, no heavy vignettes, no film grain. Photos are never green-tinted. If a photo needs more correction than this to look right, it's the wrong photo. Frame: media radius radius-m. A photo sits on paper or ink surfaces, never on a pattern surface — one texture per band. Photo and pattern never share a band. Two photo surfaces per viewport at most.

What we shoot, and what we never shoot. Working sessions mid-conversation — whiteboards, marked-up plans, laptops shared Posed handshakes, suits at glass towers, skyline panoramas — the category code we break Hands doing the work; rooms as they actually are Green-tinting or duotoning photos — the one-color discipline lives in UI, pattern and type Natural or available light; subjects off-center, room to breathe Staged "diversity grid" stock energy; anything that couldn't be a real Tuesday Client teams alongside ours — dignity, never surveillance candid Photography as wallpaper — two photo surfaces per viewport at most

Interim stock, then owned shoots. Now — curated stock Free candid sources (Pexels) only, passed through the do and don't filter above. Every placeholder carries a credit link. Stock is scaffolding — it holds the layout, it doesn't define the brand. Before launch — the shoot list One documentary half-day covers the site: a working session at the board a client-side pairing over one laptop hands on a printed plan the room, empty, lights on Shot flat, graded with the recipe, done.

We don't draw — with two sanctioned exceptions. Photography, the pattern and the icon set carry all meaning. No new drawing practice exists: no character mascots, isometric scenes, 3D blobs, hand-drawn doodles or AI spot art — anywhere. The policy was adopted on 2026-07-16. The floor is the rule. The two extensions below are the only exceptions, and both reuse languages the system already owns. Pattern as spot art Seeded crops of <khyzr-pattern> only — never redrawn shapes. One spot per surface, its seed fixed and logged. Scope: empty states, 404, email headers, deck section breaks. The pattern caps hold: two pattern surfaces per viewport at most, never behind long copy. The spots in use, with their fixed seeds: Empty state dark 23 0.5 404 medallion (circle) dark 8 0.45 Email header light 41 0.5 Line diagrams — explanatory only Flows, systems, timelines — things that explain, in decks, docs and proposals. Stroke 1.5 in currentColor, kin to the Solar icons: forest on light, green-300 on dark. Radii from the locked set. Labels in Manrope, the technical register (font-tech). Terracotta flags the one thing to see, as on the Data page (signal). Never decorative, never on the website hero.
Paper cutouts in the brand greens — generative, seeded, always deliberate. This is the website's texture, and it dresses sections and elements, never whole pages.

Two themes, one component. The pattern is a single element, <khyzr-pattern>, from khyzr-pattern.js in the design system's pattern assets. Production uses this asset. It was adopted as the official website texture on 2026-07-13. The element is static, deterministic and sized by its container. Any number of instances share one WebGL context. Without WebGL it paints a quiet solid fill in its theme's canvas color. Dark is the default and its look is locked: the green-900 canvas, with the palette shapes composited at 10% and pre-flattened. Text is safe on it as it is. Light is grayscale, at 50% strength on a #E9E9E9 canvas. Text on it stays at body or darker, and long-form copy needs a solid panel. Seeded means the same composition on every load. Attributes theme dark (the default) or light seed any number; sets a deterministic composition (default 7) scale cutout size multiplier, sensible from 0.5 to 2 (default 1) animate when present, a slow ambient drift — moved by CSS transform only, with no re-rendering, and off automatically under reduced motion Place the element absolutely, filling a positioned container that clips its overflow, and set the content above it. Do and don't Hero bands, CTA cards, stat strips, dividers, footer caps Full-page backgrounds — it's seasoning, not the plate Card media slots and empty states Long-form body copy on the light theme without a solid panel Set text directly on the dark theme — shapes are 10% tints, quiet by design Recoloring, gradients on top, or mixing themes in one section Pick a seed per surface and keep it — compositions are part of the design More than two pattern surfaces in a viewport Sections, cards, media slots and dividers — never the page background. Never recolor. The themes are the only variations. A photo and the pattern never share a band.

The dark hero band: dark theme, seed 7, scale 1. No scrim needed — the copy sits straight on the pattern. The headline is Outfit at the display weight (fw-display), in on-dark-heading. The calls to action are the white button and the hero ghost button from Components.

Stat strip Dark theme, seed 33, scale 0.8 — a finer field under small type. Numbers in Outfit 600 at 46px. One accent figure at most, in green-300. Section divider Dark theme, seed 5, scale 0.6, 110px high. Label only — a divider never carries body copy.

Pattern as card media, shown on the service cards. The media cap is 150px high: dark theme, seeds 11, 23 and 31, scale 0.7. One seed per card, fixed. Siblings must differ. The card body stays on solid white.

CTA card Light theme, seed 21, scale 0.85, radius radius-l. Short copy only on the light pattern — headings, and ink text at body or darker. Pull quote Light theme, seed 40, scale 0.9. Instrument Serif italic is the page's one serif accent (the Voice rule).
The closing band. Dark theme, seed 3, scale 1.2 — a calmer, larger field. The on-dark wordmark at 34px high. The legal row in on-dark-faint.

One seed per surface, fixed — the compositions are part of the design. These are the seeds and scales in use. Theme samples dark and light 7 1 Hero band dark 7 1 Stat strip dark 33 0.8 Section divider dark 5 0.6 Service cards dark 11 · 23 · 31 0.7 CTA card light 21 0.85 Pull quote light 40 0.9 Footer cap dark 3 1.2
The Green Trace — things grow in. The curves, clocks and rules for everything that moves.

khyzr's motion behaves like growth. Elements rise crisp from their own baseline — scale anchored at the ground line, a breath of overshoot — and overlap as they enter. Never a queue, never a flicker, never out of focus. Adopted on 2026-07-14. It serves a line from the voice: "When we leave, things should be growing that weren't before."

Four rules, no exceptions. Springs move things, never colors. Overshoot curves apply to transforms only. Color, background and opacity change on plain ease — a hue can't bounce. Entrances overlap. Grouped elements start one dur-stagger apart, while the previous one is still moving — growth, not a queue. Nothing animates twice. One arrival per element per page view. Re-entering a section does not replay it. Ambient loops (marquee, quotes) are the only repeaters. Motion is a privilege. Reduced motion gets final states instantly — no autoplay, and hovers keep working without transforms. No GPU means static fallbacks, never a broken sim.

Curves and clocks. Curves ease-trace entrances and big moves — a soft spring, slight overshoot ease-pop hovers and pulses — a livelier overshoot for small distances ease-drift growing bars and widths — decisive, no overshoot (a bar can't shrink past zero) plain ease, 200–350ms color, background, border, opacity — including the nav paper-flip Clocks dur-enter entrances dur-stagger the stagger step, overlapping dur-hover hovers dur-pulse the settle pulse dur-count count-ups Distances Rise: rise-distance. Entrance scale: from rise-scale to 1, anchored at the baseline (the element's bottom center). Card lift: −3px, with a −.4° tilt and scale 1.015. Button grow: 1.05. Settle pulse: 1.07.

The four moves. Section entrance Entrances run on ease-trace over dur-enter: a rise of rise-distance and a scale up from rise-scale, grown from the baseline. Crisp the whole way — no blur, no filter. Overlapping stagger When several elements enter together, each starts one dur-stagger after the last, overlapping the one before it. Count-up and settle pulse Numbers count up over dur-count, then land with a settle pulse to 1.07 on ease-pop over dur-pulse. Hovers Hovers run on ease-pop over dur-hover. Buttons grow to 1.05. Cards grow toward you: they lift −3px, tilt −.4° and scale to 1.015.

What moves how on the homepage. Section reveals ease-trace over dur-enter — rise and scale anchored at the baseline; a dur-stagger overlap when several enter together Proof numbers count over dur-count, ease-out, with a settle pulse of 1.07 on landing; reduced motion keeps the final values in the markup Cards on hover, lift −3px, tilt −.4° and scale 1.015, on ease-pop over dur-hover Buttons and arrows grow to scale 1.05 on ease-pop over dur-hover; arrows slide 4px on the same curve; ghost buttons stay color-only Nav paper-flip plain ease, 350ms, at 72% of the hero — a color and surface change, so no spring Ambient clocks the marquee runs 30s linear; the quote rotation advances every 8s and pauses on hover — exempt from "nothing animates twice" Scroll-driven pieces and simulations the manifesto word-scrub and the hero gradient and liquid word follow the scroll or the pointer, not a clock — outside this grammar; they keep their reduced-motion and no-GPU fallbacks
Every pattern on the site, recreated one to one — actions, navigation, the section header, cards and bands, accents, proof and voices, and the footer. The rules sit with each pattern.

Every button is a pill, radius-pill — never a square button. The primary CTA reads "Book a conversation", always; never "Get started", "Learn more" or "Contact us". Primary — the ink pill with white text. It is the default. Secondary, on light — a transparent pill with a hairline border. On hover the border darkens and the fill turns white. Text link — ink text with an arrow that slides 4px on hover. On dark bands — the white pill leads on green-900 and ink. The hero ghost is white at 8% with a light blur and a white border at 36%; the footer ghost is a white border at 25% that brightens to 60% on hover. Ghost — the outlined pill lives on dark surfaces only, never on light. Hover — buttons grow 1.05 on ease-pop over dur-hover, and arrows slide on the same curve. Ghost buttons stay color-only. Focus — a 2px focus-ring outline at a 3px offset; white on dark. A quiet reassurance aside can sit under a CTA — one of the voice's signature moves.

The paper-flip bar: full width, fixed, 64px tall, set on the container's gutters. It has two states and one change between them. Over the hero Transparent, with no border. Links are white at 78%, going full white on a faint white plate on hover. The CTA is the white pill. Past the hero Once the page scrolls past 72% of the hero's height, the bar flips to paper at 97% with a hairline below. It stays shadowless. Links are muted, going ink on a surface-2 plate on hover. The CTA flips to the ink pill. Both states The flip is a color and surface change on standard ease (350ms) — never a spring. The brand is the wordmark, at least 90px wide, crossfading from on-dark to on-light: the wordmark leads wherever the name fits (see Logos). The CTA reads "Book a conversation" in both states. The glass and green-900 bars are retired.

Eyebrow, then title, then lede — the way every section opens. The eyebrow is numbered, in the technical register, behind the green dash: "01 · What we do". On dark it turns green-bright. The title sets at text-title, tracked tight at tracking-display. One green word per title, at most — the payoff word. The lede sets at text-lede in muted, held to measure-lede. The header block runs to 760px wide, with 44–72px of fluid space below it.

The containers. Discipline grid — hairline cells Cells sit in a grid whose 1px gaps are painted by the hairline behind them. The outer corner is radius-l; cells fill minmax(290px, 1fr). A cell rests on surface-2 and lifts to white on hover, while a 20px green tick slides out beside its title. Each cell carries a numeral, 01 to 06, in the technical register, then a title and one line in muted. Partner card — lifts on hover White surface, a hairline border, radius-m, 30px padding. A green lane label in the technical register sits above the name and a one-line description. On hover the card lifts −3px, tilts −.4° and scales 1.015 on ease-pop, and takes the soft hover shadow. Cards run in a grid of minmax(240px, 1fr) with an 18px gap. Statement band — ink and a green bloom An ink ground at radius-l, with a soft radial green bloom in the upper right. Text in on-dark-soft, the bold phrase in white, one highlight in green-bright, on-dark-accent. Principle item — ruled top Each principle sits under a 2px hairline rule: a title, then one line in muted. The lead variant takes a green rule — it marks the anchor principle. Principles run in a grid of minmax(180px, 1fr), gap 36 / 30.

A small vocabulary. Pillar chips — a word at display weight, led by a 7px green dot. Scroll cue — a 1×32px bar fading downward, pulsing on a 2.4s cycle, above a technical label. Accent phrase — the payoff words of a line in green. Status chips The Badge primitive is the system's chip grammar for status — not the logo badge. Solid is decided or locked, outline is status, neutral is quiet meta, mint is an ID chip. Mint sets deep forest text on pale mint. Never green-600 on mint at small sizes.

The proof band and client quotes. Proof stats — the count-up pair A light band with a hairline below. A pair of display-scale numerals, each with its unit mark in green and a caption in the technical register, set off from the logo row by a hairline divider. Numbers count up from zero on first reveal over dur-count and land with a settle pulse of 1.07. Under reduced motion they show their final values. Client logos roll beside them in a 30-second marquee, dark on transparent on the light band. Voices — the rotating quote band Green-900 at radius-l, with the dark <khyzr-pattern> on one fixed seed, centered. The quote sets in Outfit at display weight, held to about 44 characters a line. Beneath it, the client's logo in white on transparent, the name in white and the role in a muted on-dark grey. Quotes advance every 8 seconds and pause on hover. The current dot is green-bright; the others are white at 24%.

The dark closing. The footer is always Ink. Top row — a headline held to 14ch with one green-bright accent word, and the footer ghost pill, "Book a conversation", with its arrow. An on-dark-divider rule runs below. Columns — the brand column at 1.4fr holds the on-dark wordmark and one line; the link columns at 1fr each are headed in the technical register in on-dark-faint. Links — on-dark-body, turning white on hover. External links sit quieter, in on-dark-muted, with the outward arrow. Base row — a green dot before the copyright line; legal links in on-dark-faint. The on-ink greys are the on-dark tokens — on-dark-body, on-dark-muted and on-dark-faint — not one-off values.
Plate fields — filled plates with no border at rest, white with a green ring on focus. Soft, roomy and quiet until you touch them.

Quiet at rest, white when awake. The plate is the affordance, so a resting field needs no border. Green appears only on focus and success — the rare-accent rule holds here too. The Plate direction was adopted on 2026-07-13. Rest — a surface-2 plate, transparent border, radius-m, padding 13 × 16. Focus — the plate turns white and takes a khyzr-green border with a soft 3px ring of green at 14%. Filled — the value sits on the resting plate. Disabled — the whole group at 45% opacity, label included. Field text is Outfit at 15px. Labels are 13px at fw-ui, always visible, above the field — no floating labels, no placeholder-as-label. Helper text sits under the field: 12.5px, faint, one line.

The same plate, every shape. Select — the plate with a chevron at the right, a 1.5-stroke line in muted. It focuses like the field. Textarea — the plate, resizing vertically. Choice pills — for a single pick. Plate-filled pills at radius-pill, each with a native radio inside. Unselected pills carry muted text and a border that shows on hover; the selected pill earns the green border and ink text. Radios and checkboxes — native controls, tinted with accent-color set to khyzr Green.

Error speaks, success nods. Error — the border turns error over a 6% wash, and the message replaces the helper line: same slot, never both. The message sets at 12.5px in error. Write error messages in voice: plain, direct, no blame. Success — a quiet green line beside the action, with a check. Not a modal, not a banner. Submit is always the existing pill, and each form has one primary action.

The dark-band companion: the same geometry, translated for green-900 — where the CTA band's booking form lives. On the primitive, set onDark. Plate — white at 8%. Focus — white at 12%, a green-bright border, a ring at 18%. Error — #E08A80 over a 10% wash. Labels set in on-dark-soft. Green-bright takes over for focus and success, matching the on-dark accent everywhere else. Submit flips to the white pill, under a white rule at 14%.

Do and don't Keep labels visible, above the field Floating labels or placeholder-as-label One primary action per form — the pill Green on anything but focus and success Let the error message replace the helper, in the same slot Borders on resting fields — the plate is the affordance Ask only what the conversation needs Toasts, modals or red banners for validation
Cobalt and signal — green carries, terracotta flags. khyzr charts say one thing at a time.

Green is always the point: series 1, the number that matters. Everything else supports — cobalt for the comparison, steel for context, and one terracotta flag when something must be seen. Terracotta is loud on purpose and rare on purpose: never a series, never mistaken for failure. The grammar is the Canopy, adopted on 2026-07-16 and recut on 2026-08-08 to the Verdant standard secondaries.

Four rules, no exceptions. Green takes series 1, always. The lead series is khyzr Green; no chart leads with an auxiliary. The greens ramp (500, 700, 800) appears only in categorical splits, never as competing series. Soft, rounded, editorial. Bars round at radius 5–6. Area fills fade from 18% to zero. Axes are single hairline rules. No 3D, no gridironed plots, no shadows-as-data. Outfit numerals, technical labels. Values set in Outfit at 600, labelled at the endpoint on the chart where possible. Axes, legends and captions are Manrope, the technical register. Proof numbers stay display-scale. Charts obey the Green Trace. Bars grow from their baseline on ease-drift; numbers count up over dur-count with the settle pulse. One arrival per chart per page view — nothing loops, nothing animates twice.

One lead, cobalt second, steel context, one signal. khyzr Green, viz-lead — series 1, always. Lines stroke Forest, viz-lead-deep, over green-500 fills; endpoint dots and the big numeral go deep. Cobalt, viz-2 — the second series: comparisons, last year, the benchmark. Cobalt is the info secondary, and text-safe on paper. Steel, viz-3 — the third series, and comparison ghosts: last year's dashed line behind this year's green. Steel tint, viz-4 — the fourth series, remainders, "everything else". Past four categories, regroup the data instead. Terracotta, signal — the signal: flags, negatives, annotations. One terracotta moment per chart, never a series, never UI chrome. Small text, and text on tints, uses the twin signal-text; signal-tint is the wash behind signal chips. Why the signal is loud The auxiliaries stay cool so green keeps the floor. The signal is exempt — rare earns loud. Terracotta is hotter than anything else on the chart, so one flag reads across the room. A flag is not a failure error stays feedback-only and never enters a chart. It is the signal's own text twin: one warm family for flags and failures, told apart by placement rather than shade. Still banned Bright leaf stays gradient-only. No auxiliary leads, and none appears without green. Links, buttons and focus rings stay green. The signal never touches chrome.

The six shapes of a khyzr chart. Trend, this year against last — the green line strokes forest over a fading fill. The comparison is steel, dashed and labelled at its endpoint — no legend box. Grouped bars, one flag — the flagged value swaps its cobalt for terracotta, once per chart. Its label uses the text twin. Split, four categories — one rounded bar. The biggest slice is green; the auxiliaries follow in weight order: cobalt, steel, steel tint. No pies, no donuts. Proof number — a deep forest numeral, a green unit mark and a caption in the technical register. It counts up over dur-count with the settle pulse. Annotation on the line — the annotation kit: a terracotta dot, a dashed riser and a short technical note. The line itself stays green. On dark — on green-900, skip cobalt: it sinks, at 2.3:1. Series run green, steel, steel tint; terracotta stays legible for marks.

Lead every chart with green; add cobalt, then the steels, in weight order Run terracotta as a series, in UI chrome, or twice in one chart Label endpoints on the chart; skip legend boxes where you can Confuse flags with failures — error states live in forms and never enter a chart Spend terracotta on the one thing the reader must see Lead with an auxiliary, or show one without green Use signal-text for terracotta text at small sizes and on tints Use cobalt on green-900 — it sinks; use steel and steel tint Regroup data past four categories — "everything else" is steel tint Draw pies, donuts, 3D or shadows-as-data — the split bar is the shape
How khyzr paper reads — two document classes, one anatomy. Duplicate a template; never restyle from scratch.

Every khyzr document is one of two kinds, and each has its template. The document — grounded, elegant, informative: guides, references, how-tos, memos. A white canvas, the wordmark in the header, and one flowing text column composed from the standard blocks. It prints on whatever paper the reader has. The brand book — spectacular, paginated, designed page by page: the Quick Guide, flagship PDFs, anything with a cover. A deep-green cover plate with a pattern column and a hero word, ghost chapter numerals, one dark statement interlude, and an Ink back cover with contact cards.

Both classes are built from the same parts. Canvas Pure White — the same canvas as the web. Dark pages use green-900; the back cover is always Ink. Page A4 or Letter, portrait (the employee Drive prints A4). Brand-book pages take 56–64px padding and full-bleed color. Documents take 0.85in margins and flow. Type scale Eyebrow: Manrope 600, 12px, .16em, uppercase, green. Title: Outfit at fw-display (600), 40–46px, −.027em. Section heads: Outfit 600, 21–24px. Body: Outfit 14–16px at 1.6. Folios and labels: Manrope 600, 11px, .10em, uppercase. One Instrument Serif italic turn per page, at most. Blocks White cards (radius-m, hairline, no shadows), definition rows split by hairlines, numbered rules, stat tiles on surface-2, and notes washed in a secondary at a 5–10% tint. Folio A hairline, then a green dot; the document name at left, the page count or contact at right, in Manrope at 11px. Covers and back covers carry the meta grid instead: RELEASE / DATE / QUESTIONS. Logos The wordmark in the header or at the cover's top left, at least 90px wide; the white badge on the back cover, which is Ink. Never compose lockups by hand. Marks sit on White, Ink or the deep green only.

Green leads every page: the eyebrows, the rules, the folio dot. The secondaries play across the content — cobalt informs, marigold warms and highlights, steel quiets, terracotta signals. Use the secondaries as washes (a 5–10% tint with a matching border), colored numerals, chips and section rules. They never become competing fields. When a secondary carries copy, it sets in its AA text twin. Ghost chapter numerals sit in green-100 at 55% opacity.

Pattern — bands, columns and panels only; the cover column is the signature print use. At most two per page, never behind body text, never a full page. Imagery — honest documentary at radius-m, never sharing a band with the pattern. Most documents need no photos: restraint is the default. Icons — Solar only. Linear beside text, in ink; Line Duotone at 32px and up, in forest — one per card or section, never more than two tones.

Exported PDFs are named Khyzr <document> (verdant-N).pdf, carrying the brand-kit release: Khyzr Quick Guide (verdant-2).pdf. Nothing is edited downstream. Every document carries its release — in the header, the cover meta or the back cover. Questions route to [cisco@khyzr.com](mailto:cisco@khyzr.com).
AI agents that run inside the client's own AWS account. khyzr.ai keeps khyzr's type and frame and brings its own colour — one periwinkle-to-aqua ramp on a near-black ground.

The two product sites are one system with two colours. What they hold in common is a vocabulary, not a design. From khyzr: the mark system. The product wordmark is the corporate wordmark with .ai; the product icon is the corporate symbol in this product's ramp. The corporate rules in [Logos](../logos/) still govern the corporate mark. With khyzr.studio: the frame, the type scale, the nav, the closing, the colophon, focus, the button skeletons and the radius ladder, shared by name and structure. Its own: colour, the hero, the engines, and every section's content. Type: Outfit only, at three weights by role — khyzr's one family, without the technical face: the product sites load no Manrope. See [Type](../type/).

Product marks follow one set of rules — icon or wordmark, never both; the icon's structure; the tiles and favicons — kept in [Logos](../logos/#product-marks). This page holds only what is this product's own. On dark: khyzr in the site's off-white, .ai in a1 #7280FC. On light: khyzr in the site's ground #070809; .ai stays a1. One color: the product wordmark in the corporate mono values, black and white. The icon cuts Dark a1 #7280FC a2 #62A5FA a4 #43F0F4 deep a2 #022853 Light a2 a1 a1 darkened #4A50C8 white

The values below are read from the khyzr.ai site's own stylesheet each time this site is built. Structure: a near-black ground in three steps — base, raised, and the console's framing band — with two hairlines, all faintly tinted toward the accent hue; two ink levels; one hue family as a four-stop ramp. The ramp is a hue sweep, periwinkle to aqua, every stop bright. a1 is the focus ring, the accent field's top rule, and the far end of lit gradients. a2 is selection, the caret, the form accent, the nav underline on hover, and the current stage's numeral. a3 is the hot stop: the accent field's fill, the primary button's hover, a stage rule on hover. a4 appears only inside gradients. Where colour lives: focus, selection and caret, link underlines on hover, the primary button's hover, rims, active and done markers, one active word, the rail segment, the index marker, the tile wash, the ripple, and one full-bleed accent field — flat a3, with the ink flipping to the ground. Strictly monochrome: all type, the nav, buttons at rest, plates and tiles at rest, hairlines, dot grids, tables, the FAQ and the footer. No gradient text; headings are always monochrome. Ratio: about 85% near-black, 3% light and 11% saturated on the hero viewport.
One family, three weights, and these sizes only. Every corner on the page reads a step of the radius ladder. The seven names and values are the same on khyzr.studio.

The values below are read from the khyzr.studio site's own stylesheet each time this site is built. Structure: a warm ground ladder, two levels and a hairline, with bone and ash for ink, and the ember ramp — an even staircase from yellow to rose, each step falling the same in lightness and in hue. The brand colour is ember-1, the .studio yellow. Every flat accent reads it: the wordmark's .studio, selection, link and nav underlines, hover borders, the offer's ticks. ember-3 is the hot stop. The ramp itself carries the gradients, the card and the bands, and the five pillars take its steps in order. Ember is a state. ease carries state changes, 300ms or less; ease-long carries arrivals.
